text: SOC 2 and ISO 27001 both show up constantly once you're in a cloud environment that handles anything sensitive, and they're structured very differently from each other. This lesson applies both of them specifically to how you configure and operate your own cloud accounts — the same real controls you've already been building in this course, now framed as audit evidence.

SOC 2 is built on AICPA standards. An independent auditor examines your controls and writes a report stating their opinion on whether those controls meet chosen Trust Services Criteria — there's no single pass/fail badge the way ISO 27001 has. A Type I report reviews whether controls were suitably designed at one point in time. A Type II report goes further, testing whether those controls actually operated effectively over a review period, typically six to twelve months, which is why serious enterprise buyers specifically ask for Type II.

SOC 2 evaluates against up to five Trust Services Criteria: Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy. Security is the only one that's mandatory in every report. The other four get scoped in based on what the organization actually does — most B2B SaaS audits end up scoping to Security, Availability, and Confidentiality, since those map most directly to what a typical SaaS customer cares about.

ISO 27001 takes a different shape entirely: it certifies your Information Security Management System, scoped to explicitly include your cloud accounts and workloads, against Annex A control areas like access control, cryptography, operations security, and your supplier relationships — including the relationship with AWS or Microsoft itself. An accredited body issues a three-year certificate, with annual surveillance audits confirming it's still being followed.

Here's the part that should feel familiar: IAM policies and enforced MFA are evidence for SOC 2 Security and ISO 27001 access control at the same time. Retained logs are evidence for both frameworks' operations controls. Encryption at rest is evidence for SOC 2 Confidentiality and ISO 27001 cryptography. You built this already — compliance work is mostly documenting it. Next lesson: the real Azure and AWS tools that map that configuration to a chosen framework automatically.
